lead_headline: Weekend restaurant tracker stays quiet — no new leads detected since Friday's modest four-lead batch

restaurant.blurb: Zero new leads this weekend. The tracker caught nothing Friday-Sunday — unusual silence after last week's steady 4-lead daily pace. Active pipeline holds at 286 leads (155 openings, 131 closures).

liquor.blurb: Day 45 of the freeze. Zero applications today — the weekend pattern holds as Monday looms. Since June 1, Colorado's licensing pipeline remains completely dormant: 274 applications flagged in the 7-day window are stale backdated corrections, not live filings. No genuine new activity in six weeks. The 12,512 tracked licenses sit frozen while the state offers no explanation. Either hospitality investment collapsed statewide simultaneously (implausible), or the licensing apparatus broke without public notice (probable). Monday marks seven full weeks without a single new application reaching the tracker.

reputation.blurb: 1 mention yesterday — Saturday's single citation came via Google News RSS. The weekend drop-off continues as expected. Week closes at 75 mentions across 16 sources, up 4% from last week's 72 and matching late June's baseline range. Denver Post led with 19 citations, followed by Instagram (15), Facebook (14), Reddit (11), Hoodline (3). Google News captured 74 of 75 (99% efficiency). Pattern holds: third consecutive week in mid-70s range, consistent sourcing diversity, stable post-holiday performance. Notable weekend pickups included San Antonio Express-News covering Tower Life redevelopment and Denver Post running Belcaro mansion sales piece.

subscriptions.blurb: Net flat yesterday (0 new, 0 canceled) — tenth consecutive day without positive growth extends July's unprecedented acquisition drought. Since Friday: net −2 (3 new, 5 canceled). MTD holds barely positive at +2 (+0.2/day), while 90-day cumulative slips to +115. The crisis deepens: July 4-13 now marks the longest zero-growth streak on record. Ten straight days without gaining ground, crushing the +1.2/day YTD baseline. Week 2 closed worse than Week 1 with 7-day net at −8 (22 new, 30 canceled) — churn accelerating while acquisition vanished. Remove June 30's carryover and July runs definitively negative through nearly two weeks. Current daily pace lags historical trend by 83%. No recovery signal emerging.
